story.label: Stamped concrete process

stages.title: Press the pattern into fresh concrete
stages.body: Stamp mats are laid on the fresh slab and pressed in, so the surface takes on stone, brick or slate texture.

stages.title: Tamp to an even depth
stages.body: Release powder keeps the mats from sticking while the pattern is tamped in evenly across the surface.

stages.title: Lift the mat to reveal the impression
stages.body: Lifting the mat shows the crisp joints and stone texture left in the surface.

stages.title: Seal the finished surface
stages.body: The finished surface is sealed. Here, a sealed grey herringbone.

items.q: How long does decorative concrete last?
items.a: With a sound sub-base and the right sealer, decorative concrete is a long-lasting surface. Lifespan depends on use, climate and maintenance.
Sweep regularly and wash with a mild cleaner. Avoid harsh acids on sealed surfaces.
Sealers wear with traffic and sun, so exposed outdoor areas are resealed more often than indoor floors.
Any concrete can develop hairline cracks. Control joints guide where movement happens, and a stamped pattern can hide joints in its lines.
Area, finish type, thickness and reinforcement, site access, base condition and sealer all affect the price. A site visit gives the most accurate quote.

items.q: How long will my project take?
items.a: It depends on size, finish and curing time. We confirm the schedule in your quote.
Slip resistance depends on the finish and sealer. Textured stamped finishes and anti-slip sealer additives are options for wet or sloped areas.

items.q: Can you pour in Jordan's summer heat?
items.a: Hot weather affects setting and curing. Pours are planned for cooler hours and the surface is protected while it cures.
